title: The Moving Average for Beginners: How to Read It, With a Real Ethereum Chart
text: Two simple lines can show you when a trend turns. Traders call it the moving average. Today: how to read it, with a real example. An indicator is simple math done on past prices. It does not see the future. It sums up the past. Each candle covers one time block, like 1 hour or 1 day. A moving average is the average close of recent candles. The 20 average is fast. The 50 average is slow. When the fast line crosses the slow line, the trend may turn. Fast below slow means sellers are taking over. Here is a real Ethereum chart from October 19. The 20 average crossed below the 50 average. That candle closed at 2,407 dollars. 5 days later, Ethereum was 2 percent lower. This time the signal worked. Never act on the moving average alone. Wait for price to confirm before you act. Always set a stop loss before you enter. Then the most you can lose is small and known. The moving average is a clue, never a promise. title: The Shooting Star Pattern for Beginners: Shape, Meaning and a Real Bitcoin Example
text: This pattern can warn you that a rise may be ending. Traders call it the shooting star. Today you learn its shape, its meaning, and how to use it. First, every candle shows four prices. The body runs from the open to the close. Each candle covers one time block, like 1 hour or 1 day. It shows up after prices rose for a while. It has a small body near the bottom. Its upper wick is long, at least 2 times the body. Buyers pushed up, but sellers pushed it back down. Here is a real Bitcoin chart from May 6. It reached 82,799 dollars. title: Hammer Candle Explained: A Real Bitcoin Example
text: This one candle can warn you that a fall may be ending. Traders call it the hammer. It has a small body near the top. Its lower wick is long, at least 2 times the body. That wick means sellers pushed the price down hard. But buyers pushed it back up before the candle closed. So the buyers won this battle. A hammer matters most at the end of a downtrend. Here is a real Bitcoin candle from September 28. It fell to 82,562 dollars. Then it closed at 83,068 dollars. Small body on top, long lower wick: a real hammer. 5 candles later, Bitcoin was 1 percent higher. Wait for the next candle to close higher. That is confirmation. Put your stop loss just below the wick. A hammer is a clue, never a promise. Watch live whale moves for free on MarketRadar Whale.
